Playbook.name: AD — KRBTGT Account Password Reset (Golden Ticket Prep / Remediation) - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access / Impact on Kerberos trust

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The krbtgt account had a password/attribute change (4724/4723/4738). This is either planned Golden Ticket remediation (krbtgt should be rotated periodically) or a suspicious touch of the domain's most sensitive account. Triage question: was this a known remediation/rotation, or an unexpected change?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: krbtgt secrets the entire Kerberos trust; unexpected changes indicate either an in-progress Golden Ticket response or tampering with domain-wide authentication.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

InitialAssessment.Rule: A scheduled krbtgt rotation by AD admins under change control is expected (and good); an unplanned change or one by an unexpected principal must be treated as incident-linked.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the krbtgt change is a controlled rotation or an unexpected/tampering event.

Step.name: Confirm the actor and exact change
Step.Purpose: Identify who touched krbtgt and how (reset vs attribute change).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "krbtgt" AND event.code IN ("4724","4723","4738","4781") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A single reset by a recognised AD admin = likely rotation. Two resets in quick succession is the recommended double-rotation for Golden Ticket eradication - confirm an incident is in progress.

Step.name: Actor's broader privileged activity
Step.Purpose: If the actor is also doing DCSync/group changes, the krbtgt touch may be attacker anti-forensics rather than remediation.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("4662","4728","4732","4756","5136") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS ops = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Actor also performing replication/group edits recontextualises the krbtgt change as part of an attack chain.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a krbtgt change with no known rotation/incident, or INV-02 shows the actor in a privileged-abuse chain.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unexpected krbtgt tamper - IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a controlled rotation by a recognised AD admin matching a change/remediation record.
Change by a plausible admin but no rotation record found.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-KRBTGT-CHANGE, INV-02-KRBTGT-ACTOR to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Planned krbtgt rotation (hygiene or Golden Ticket remediation) under change control.

Indicators.Item: Matches a rotation schedule or active IR runbook.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the rotation record; close as false_positive; ensure the second rotation (if remediation) is scheduled.

TruePositive.Definition: Unexpected manipulation of the krbtgt secret.

Indicators.Item: Actor unexpected or in an abuse chain.

SOCAction.Item: Engage IR: treat as possible domain compromise.
Verify DC integrity; plan controlled double rotation as part of eradication.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automation/script rotating krbtgt outside the sanctioned process.

Indicators.Item: A scripted account performing the reset off-schedule.

SOCAction.Item: Align rotation with the sanctioned process; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm whether an IR/rotation is in progress.
If unexpected: engage IR and verify DC integrity.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: If compromise suspected: controlled krbtgt double-rotation, privileged resets, ticket revocation.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Adopt a scheduled krbtgt rotation policy with change control.

QualityChecks.Check: krbtgt changes are rare - every instance warrants confirmation against change management.
A legitimate double-rotation looks alarming; corroborate with the AD team.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: If TP: eradication completed, double rotation done, tickets revoked.
